title: Pearl Harbor night at Enrico's
summary: On the night of Pearl Harbor he was playing a female-impersonator floor show at Enrico's, and he also did taxi dances.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: I'll never forget December the seventh, the night that the Japanese had bombed Pearl Harbor. I was working at a place called Enrico's over on Rivard(?) and Watson. And people came running in the place, shouting 'We're at war! We're at war! We're at war!' I never thought of anything like that, you know. And we had a nice band in there, playing for the floor show. We had an all female impersonator floor show.

I was really getting plenty of experiences in Detroit, you know... [HEARTY LAUGH] I even played some taxi dances, and I did some nightclub work out in Dearborn, where they had a chorus line and everything -- I don't remember the name of the place. And I was just adding to the
experiences. And I'd still go by the Bandbox and play with the guys, you know, because that kept you sharp and kept your name alive, and you'd start growing.
